name: 84 Hours Anoxic Naturals
description:

After fermentation, the mucilage remains as the beans are dried on raised beds or patios under controlled conditions for even drying. 
 Located in Chikmagalur, Sai Ashirwad estate is renowned for growing various coffees, including Arabica SLN 795,CxR and Robusta Old Peridenia. The farm has organic certification, showcasing its commitment to sustainable practices. Beyond coffee, it is a haven for wildlife like Indian Gaur and Malabar Giant squirrels. The estate features its own processing unit and drying yards to ensure careful handling of beans. Additionally, water harvesting ponds reflect their focus on environmental stewardship.

name: Excelsa community
description:
We hand-pick fully ripe, deep red cherries with high sugar content, ensuring minimal defects and consistent quality. After harvesting, cherries are sorted in water; ripe cherries sink while underripe or damaged ones float and are removed.  Sorted cherries are spread in thin layers on raised beds in a ventilated polyhouse, which controls temperature and protects against rain and UV exposure. We turn the cherries manually to ensure even drying and prevent fermentation. Regular raking promotes airflow, enhancing the final flavor. In the evenings, cherries are covered to shield them from moisture. We monitor moisture levels, aiming for 11–12% to preserve flavors and minimize microbial risks. After drying, cherries are packed in jute sacks and stored for at least two months to stabilize and mature. 
 The Mooleh Manay estate is situated near the scenic backwaters of the Harangi Reservoir in Coorg, Karnataka. It employs a data-oriented strategy for farming and coffee processing, as it believes that data plays a crucial role in enhancing agricultural practices and achieving top-quality coffee production. The estate grows various coffee types, such as Arabica, Robusta, and Excelsa, and utilizes careful processing techniques to highlight the finest flavors. The estate is dedicated to ongoing improvement and innovation and engages in research focused on indigenous Indian Coffea species and soil health.
